title: Stop! In the Name of Flaws: Disentangling Personal Names and Sociodemographic Attributes in NLP
benchmark_measurement: The paper critiques the methodological and ethical issues of using personal names to infer sociodemographic attributes, including religion. It does not propose or measure a specific benchmark but warns against the invalidity and potential harms of such practices, such as for persecuted religious groups.
findings: The paper argues that using names as a proxy for religion is methodologically flawed and ethically problematic. It highlights that religious names are used globally, which undermines simple inference, and warns that name-based classification can threaten the safety of persecuted religious groups.
